headers.comment: A company logo is written once under a name derived from the company and never edited - a new logo would be a new file. That makes it the one thing here that is genuinely immutable, and it is also the bulk of the bytes, so it is where caching actually pays.

app.js and styles.css are NOT content-hashed, so they cannot be cached immutably without risking a stale site after a deploy. stale-while-revalidate gets the repeat-visit speed anyway: the browser paints from cache immediately and refreshes in the background, so a visitor is at most one page load behind.
